messages.subject: identification in ordinal cfa
parts:
Hi,

I have looked but cannot find (I may have missed it) what default constraints Lavaan places upon ordinal CFA models in order to identify the model. It looks like the latent intercepts are constrained to zero among other things. But I wouldn't mind confirmation as to what exactly is being done - I am likely to miss something. If there is a formal reference too that would help as I would likely cite something in a manuscript.

Thanks!
John

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: identification in ordinal cfa
parts:
On 06/19/2013 06:22 PM, John Taylor wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I have looked but cannot find (I may have missed it) what default
> constraints Lavaan places upon ordinal CFA models in order to identify
> the model.

The short answer is: the same as Mplus when parameterization=delta.

A formal reference is:

Muth�n, B. (1984). A general structural equation model with dichotomous,
ordered categorical, and continuous latent variable indicators.
Psychometrika, 49(1), 115-132.

but for the multiple-group case, see also:

Muth�n, B., & Christoffersson, A. (1981). Simultaneous factor analysis
of dichotomous variables in several groups. Psychometrika, 46(4), 407-419.

Under the 'delta' parameterization, the residual variances of the
categorical indicators are NOT estimated. They are not fixed to 1 either
(a common misconception), but their values are a function of other
parameter values. The mean of the latent response (y*) is fixed to zero,
while the thresholds are freely estimated.

In the multiple-group case, 'scaling factors' are also introduced. By
default, they are fixed to 1.0 for the first group, but they can be
freely estimated in the other groups if the thresholds and factor
loadings are held fixed across groups.

Yves.

messages.author: fbde11873d6580ef
messages.subject: Re: identification in ordinal cfa
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I am estimating a CFA model of 2 common factors, each with 19 ordered categorical indicators. The model runs without problems, but when I want to include residual covariances between a number of latent response variables (19 residual covariances in total), I get the following warning:

In lavaan(unimodel.long.ord, data = BSI.ord, int.ov.free = T, int.lv.free = T,  :
 lavaan WARNING: residual covariance matrix is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.ov") to investigate.

Inspection of the residual covariance matrix shows the matrix just like I would expect it (positive, non-zero values on the diagonal, and 19 additional positive non-zero values). In addition, all other parameters values (loadings, thresholds, latent (co)variances, latent means) have plausible values as well.

My questions: Should I distrust the results of my analysis because the residual covariance matrix is not positive definite? Is there a well-known cause for the residual covariance matrix not being positive definite in the analysis of ordered categorical data?

Marjolein

John

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: identification in ordinal cfa
parts:
On 09/12/2013 01:19 PM, Marjolein Fokkema wrote:
> My questions: Should I distrust the results of my analysis because the
> residual covariance matrix is not positive definite? Is there a
> well-known cause for the residual covariance matrix not being positive
> definite in the analysis of ordered categorical data?

Try this:

eigen( inspect(fit, "cov.ov") )$values

The last value will be negative (triggering the warning). If the value
is very close to zero (say |x| < 0.00001), you can safely ignore it. If
not, this may be symptom of misfit (in your case: the estimated value
for the residual covariance may be too high, given the values of the
residual variances).

Yves.
